title: AI and Business
overview: A formal concentration within the BS in Business Administration, with one required course and three independent elective groups. The concentration requires at least 36 CMU units beyond the Business Core. This is a path within the host BS, not a separate degree.

requirements.title: No double counting

requirements.title: Additional-major waiver is not completion of this concentration
requirements.summary: The Business Administration BS ordinarily requires a concentration. Students completing an additional major may waive the concentration and minor requirements and complete 27 business-elective units in place of the concentration. That host-degree waiver does not award the named AI and Business concentration; completing this concentration requires its published four-course, minimum-36-unit plan.

requirements.title: Concentration overlap limit
requirements.summary: For Business Administration majors, concentration and business-elective courses cannot double count toward other degree requirements, including a minor or additional major. This concentration does not certify completion of the host BS.

requirements.title: Required-course letter grades and repeat treatment
requirements.summary: Required degree courses need A–D letter grades. P is permitted for Core @ CMU and the expressly named Spring 2020 / Spring 2026 CMUQ special elections; those historical exceptions do not create a current concentration pass/fail option. Repeated courses retain both grades in QPA. The host degree requires cumulative QPA of at least 2.0; no separate concentration QPA threshold is stated here.

requirements.title: Shared concentration/business-elective transfer cap
requirements.summary: At most one external course may apply across the concentration and business-elective requirements together, after Tepper equivalency review. Normally C− or higher is required unless an individual approval specifies otherwise. CMU Washington Semester and CMU-Qatar courses are exempt from this transfer policy; online/community-college courses depend on department policy. Tepper dual-degree students follow the primary-major transfer policy. The host degree also has broader transfer limits; these local observations do not approve any individual transfer.

requirements.title: Dual degree differs from an additional major
requirements.summary: A Business Administration dual degree still requires a concentration. The primary/dual degree can replace the other program’s minor when completed no later than that degree. This is distinct from the additional-major concentration waiver stated on the BS page; neither route automatically awards this named AI concentration.

requirements.title: No independent-study replacement of a required course
requirements.summary: Independent study cannot replace an existing catalog course or a curriculum requirement. Its general availability is not an unlisted AI concentration elective permission.

requirements.title: Host-degree residency context
requirements.summary: The bachelor’s degree requires at least four full-time semesters (or part-time equivalent) and 180 CMU units; more restrictive college rules may apply and deviations require the home-college dean. This is a host-degree condition, not an extra 180-unit concentration or a claim that the full BS inventory is mapped.

requirements.title: Official transfer records
requirements.summary: Transfer credit requires an official final college/university transcript and applicable college/department approval. External transfer grades do not enter the CMU QPA, whereas university cross-registration grades do. This does not waive the Tepper shared one-course concentration/business-elective transfer cap.

requirements.title: Host-degree credit age
requirements.summary: Units used toward the undergraduate degree must normally have been earned within eight years of graduation. The college dean may extend the period under the published course-relevance, preparation and legitimate-delay conditions; exceptions are not automatic.

requirements.title: Declaration timing recommendation
requirements.summary: The Business major offers this concentration and encourages declaration by the end of sophomore year. This is a recommendation, not a published eligibility deadline. Concentration selection is discussed with the academic advisor; no independent admission test or automatic transcript notation is inferred.

requirements.title: Regular academic advising
requirements.summary: Tepper students are expected to meet their academic advisor at least once each semester to select courses and review progress. The concentration catalog also directs consultation when selecting a concentration.

notes: The catalog uses BA in its no-double-counting sentence to mean Business Administration; the host award heading is BS. No BA award is inferred.
No launch date or transcript notation has been established. Other CMU AI degrees and the AI minor are distinct records.

Local concentration inventory reviewed completely on 2026-10-11: four selections from nine nine-unit subjects satisfy the 36-unit minimum; applicable grade, overlap, transfer, declaration/advising and host-degree relationship/residency policies are represented. This does not certify the complete Tepper BS curriculum or any student’s eligibility.

No description or prerequisite is inferred from a course title. All nine course unit amounts were observed; five course blocks state prerequisite expressions and absent expressions remain unknown. No course-offering guarantee, independent transcript recognition or launch date is inferred.
